faq.q: Which exam presets are built in and do they give a pass/fail?
faq.a: Seven presets set duration, language, and difficulty and then judge your result: SSC CHSL English (35 WPM, 10 min), SSC CHSL Hindi (30 WPM), SSC CGL DEO (8000 KDPH, 15 min), Court Stenographer English (40 WPM) and Hindi (30 WPM), UPPCL Typist Hindi (25 WPM), and RRB NTPC English (30 WPM). After the test it shows a PASS or FAIL verdict against that preset's requirement.

faq.q: What's the difference between Net WPM, Gross WPM, and KDPH?
faq.a: Gross WPM is characters typed divided by 5, per minute. Net WPM subtracts your error count from that before dividing, so mistakes lower it. KDPH is keystrokes per hour (including backspaces), which is the metric SSC CGL DEO is scored on. The results screen reports all of these plus accuracy, keystrokes, errors, and time.

faq.q: Can I practise in Hindi or with my own text?
faq.a: Yes. Choose Hindi to type Devanagari passages (the tool relies on your OS keyboard; a built-in guide explains enabling Inscript or Remington layouts). The Custom Text button lets you paste your own passage to practise, useful for exam-specific material. Difficulty has three levels — easy, medium, hard — and passages are shuffled and combined for longer durations.

faq.q: Does it save my scores or give a certificate?
faq.a: Your best scores are stored locally under the key typingLB and ranked by WPM (top 15 kept, top 10 shown). After finishing you can enter your name and download a PNG certificate showing Net WPM, Gross WPM, accuracy, KDPH, language, mode, date, and a pass/fail line if a preset was active. Correct characters turn green and errors red as you type.
